question: Why did the error rate go up on 16 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: New deployment caused increased error rate and latency.
why_chain: Checkout v4.18 was deployed to us-east, which likely introduced the error.
The deployment occurred 225 minutes before the error rate spike, suggesting it was the cause.
The error rate and latency increased after the deployment, indicating the deployment was the root cause.

ruled_out.reason: Request volume increased by 24%, but the error rate increased by 1044%, indicating a more significant issue.
No evidence directly links a configuration change to the error.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Data quality issues caused the error.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence suggests the error was caused by bad input data.
No evidence suggests the error was caused by server, network, or capacity issues.
No other plausible explanations are supported by the evidence.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service catalog rose from 0.36% to 4.12% (+1044%), with a change point at 2026-03-16T09:15:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service catalog: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.13).
At the same time, request volume for service catalog stayed about the same (1617 per 5 min before, 2010 per 5 min after, +24%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service catalog rose (121 ms before, 217 ms after, +80%).
catalog: ERROR upstream catalog-db timeout after 3 retries (catalog, ap-south; 14 min after the change; record R011)
catalog: ERROR upstream catalog-db timeout after 3 retries (catalog, us-east; 20 min after the change; record R012)
catalog-db status page: investigating degraded performance (catalog; 30 min after the change; record R014)
catalog: ERROR upstream catalog-db timeout after 3 retries (catalog, eu-west; 24 min after the change; record R013)
Deployed checkout v4.18 to us-east (routine release) (checkout, us-east; 225 min before the change; record R010)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 225 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✗ It concerns a different service/region than the one that changed.
✓ 3 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change
Change records for the affected service/region

actions.action: Rollback the checkout v4.18 deployment to us-east.
Monitor catalog-db for any further issues and ensure it is performing optimally.
Review and optimize the service catalog's error handling and retry mechanisms.
